status_summary: On 2025-02-14 the NLRB Acting General Counsel issued GC 25-05, permanently rescinding the 2024 memorandum on 10(j) relief after Starbucks v. McKinney and rescinding three earlier 10(j) memoranda pending further guidance, which runs against the recommendation to expand 10(j) use. On 2026-08-26 the General Counsel issued GC 26-04, which lists Board precedents the General Counsel has asked or intends to ask the Board to revisit, including the 2023 Stericycle work-rules standard and the 2023 protected concerted activity decision Miller Plastic, and discusses Lion Elastomers II, pending on remand before the Board. The memorandum does not mention Alstate Maintenance, Section 10(j) or delegation, and no Board decision returning to the 2019 standard was found.

title: Return to the 2019 protected concerted activity standard and expand 10(j) injunction use
uncertainties: GC 25-05 was read from a copy hosted on DocumentCloud, not the NLRB website. GC 26-04 was read from a copy hosted on a law firm's site; that copy carries the agency's memorandum header, number, date and signature and no firm branding, and an NLRB news release confirms the memorandum's number, date and issuer. The NLRB-hosted copy of the memorandum and the nlrb.gov memo listing could not be fetched. The law-firm blog is kept as a secondary source. Whether the General Counsel has issued new 10(j) guidance since GC 25-05, or the Board has decided a relevant case, was not found; only a limited search was run and no Board decision database was queried. The 2019 Alstate Maintenance standard was displaced by a 2023 Board decision, which was not opened. The two parts of the recommendation point in different directions: the concerted-activity part shows General Counsel positions in line with it, while the 10(j) part shows a step against it.
